label: input s at original positions 3-5
explanation: Fires only when the input token is s during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. It never fires on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase. Position matters: activity is zero at t=0-2 and t>=7, peaks at t=4 (53% of mass), and is weaker at t=3 and t=5, with a small tail at t=6 (1.3% of mass). The predicate s-at-t3..5 covers 99% of activation mass, but only about half of those steps actually fire (precision 0.48). Whether it fires depends on which tokens came earlier, in a graded way. The largest activations come when q came earlier, especially as the first token (every top example starts with q; first-token-q gives precision 0.998). Earlier q/w/u/a/0/2/y/d/b raise the firing rate (precision 0.61, F1 0.73 when combined with the position predicate). Repeat occurrences of s fire less often. No crisp rule for the history dependence was found.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: s, -, w, o, j, y; least: h, 3, l, <DEL>) and the first original token (most: q, w, u, 2, y, a; least: f, j, z, r); timing cues that raise it most: t=4, t=5, t=3.
